monthly_review.summary: This month shows a sharp drop in volume and intensity compared to last month, with only one run completed so far — likely reflecting reduced training load or recovery focus. Aerobic efficiency remains stable, but cadence and zone distribution suggest less dynamic effort.
monthly_review.highlight: The runner’s Zone 4 and Zone 5 time dropped from 19% last month to just 2% this month — indicating a near-complete absence of threshold or high-intensity work so far.

goal_tracker.message: You need 33.4 more km across 8 additional sessions in the remaining 28 days to match last month’s volume — averaging ~4.2 km per session.

insights.title: Stable but not improving efficiency
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency declined slightly from 13.66 to 13.57 m/sec per bpm, and VO2 max remained flat at 35–36 mL/kg/min across all recent runs — suggesting no recent aerobic stimulus strong enough to drive adaptation.

insights.title: Loss of higher-intensity stimulus
insights.body: Zone 4+ time fell from 19% (15% Z4 + 4% Z5) in April to just 2% Z4 and 0% Z5 in May — meaning no threshold or VO2 max efforts yet this month, which risks detraining at faster paces.

insights.title: Cadence and stride length variability signals fatigue or pacing inconsistency
insights.body: Cadence dropped to 87 spm on 2026-04-26 (a very slow 14:00 min/km effort), while peaking at 150 spm on 2026-04-22 (7:08 min/km) — a 63 spm swing across recent runs, and stride length varied from 75.3 cm to 91.8 cm, indicating inconsistent neuromuscular coordination.

insights.title: Low ground contact time and vertical oscillation suggest efficient recovery runs
insights.body: Ground contact time averaged 301–327 ms and vertical oscillation stayed between 6.4–8.8 cm across recent runs — well within healthy recreational ranges, confirming easy runs are genuinely easy and physiologically restorative.

recommendations.action: Do a 5km Zone 2 run (HR 125–135 bpm) on your next run, focusing on holding cadence ≥140 spm throughout.
recommendations.reason: Your April Zone 2 time was only 32%, and current cadence is down to 133 spm — this rebuilds aerobic base consistency while reinforcing neuromuscular rhythm.

recommendations.action: Add one 12-minute Zone 3 interval session this week: 3 × 4 minutes @ 145–152 bpm with 90 sec easy jog recovery.
recommendations.reason: Your Zone 3 contribution dropped from 26% in April to 27% this month — but with zero Z4/Z5, adding structured Zone 3 will safely raise lactate threshold without overstressing recovery.

recommendations.action: Perform a 3km 'efficiency check' run at 7:30–7:45 min/km (510–525 sec/km) with real-time cadence target of 145 spm and stride length >85 cm.
recommendations.reason: Your best recent pace was 428 sec/km (7:08 min/km) on 2026-04-22, but stride length has since dipped below 85 cm — this session reconnects speed, form, and efficiency.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish rhythm and responsiveness in Zone 2–3 while retraining neuromuscular coordination for efficient turnover and stride length — prioritizing quality over quantity after a low-volume start to May.
suggested_sessions: Zone 2 endurance run (5km, HR 125–135 bpm, cadence ≥140 spm)
Efficiency-focused tempo run (3km @ 510–525 sec/km, cadence 145 spm, stride >85 cm)
